questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

The patient remembers his son taking him to the temple.

options.text: The patient remembers he was taken to the temple by his son.
The patient remembers taken to the temple by his son.
The patient remembers himself being taken to the temple by his son.
The patient remembers being taken to the temple by his son.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**The patient remembers being taken to the temple by his son**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer is **4) The patient remembers being taken to the temple by his son.**
 
• This answer can be inferred from the rules of passive voice :
 
 
• To form the passive voice, we use a form of the verb be with a past participle.
 
• The tense of the verb depends on the tense of the active voice sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in **present simple tense**, so we use **is **or **are **in the **passive voice**, depending on the subject.
 
• The subject is the patient, which is **singular**, so we use **is**.
 
 
 
• The **past participle** of take is taken, so we use **that **after is.
 
• If we want to show the doer of the action, we use **by **followed by the agent. The agent is** his son,** so we use **by his son** at the end.
 
• The other options are incorrect because:
 
 
• **Option 1** changes the tense of the sentence from present simple to past simple. It should use is instead of was.
 
• **Option 2** omits the verb be, which is necessary for the passive voice. It should use is before taken.
 
• **Option 3** adds an unnecessary pronoun himself, which does not agree with the subject the patient. It should omit himself.
 
 

**​Correct Sentence:**__ *The patient remembers being taken to the temple by his son.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.**

Construction plays a central role in transforming the natural environment into the built environment, and many considerations and restrictions can apply before a project is given __consent__ to proceed in terms of how it may influence the environment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Interdiction**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An ***antonym***, unlike a synonym, is a word in the same language with the exact opposite meaning.
 
• The term is derived from the Greek words "anti" and "onym," which mean "***opposite***" and "name," accordingly.
 
• ***Consent*** is described as** the acceptance of something.**
 
• ***Interdiction*** is** the act of restricting or refusing something.**
 
• Therefore, '**interdiction**' is the ***antonym*** of '**consent**'. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Bickering - **argue about petty and trivial matters. (छोटी-छोटी बातों पर बहस करना)
 
• **Expulsion - **the action of forcing someone to leave an organization. (किसी को संगठन छोड़ने के लिए मजबूर करने की क्रिया)
 
• **Directive - **an official or authoritative instruction. (एक आधिकारिक निर्देश)
 
 
 
• The antonym of Bickering is ***Agree***.
 
• The antonym of Expulsion is ***Inclusion***.
 
• The antonym of Directive is ***Neglect***.

questions.question:
**Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.**

A great transition / marked / the 20th century / for mankind

options.text: A great transition marked the 20th century for mankind.
The 20th century marked a great transition for mankind.
A great transition for mankind marked the 20th century.
For mankind, a great transition marked the 20th century.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**The 20th**** century marked a great transition for mankind**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A ***meaningful sentence*** is one that uses details to clarify the meaning of a term.
 
• A relevant sentence demonstrates that the author knows the word's meaning and can apply it in a ***communicative context***.
 
• The first part would be** "the 20th century" **which starts the sentence and acts as the subject.
 
• The second part would be **"marked" **which acts as the verb of the sentence.
 
• The third part would be **"A great transition" **which will act as the object of the sentence.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

**The​​ *complete sentence* is:__ ***The 20th century marked a great transition for mankind.​*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• A*** sentence*** is a group or combination of words.
 
• To make sense, the words must be placed in a coherent order that includes ***subject + verb + object + predicate***.
 
• The relevant sentence must also be ***grammatically correct***.

questions.question:
**Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.**

The secretary assures the audience that he/she is going to help them.

options.text: The secretary said to the audience, “I am going to help you.”
The secretary says to the audience, “I am going to help you.”
The secretary says to the audience, “I was going to help you.”
The secretary says to the audience, “I will be going to help you.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"The secretary says to the audience, “I am going to help you."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **Ind**irect Speech. As per the given question we have to change it into direct Speech. 
 
• The process of transformation is as follows: 
 
 
• The reported verb is in the present tense, therefore,** 'says'** will be used in the direct speech.
 
• The conjunction '**that**' is removed and inverted commas are added.
 
• The pronoun **'he/she' **changes to** 'I'.**
 
• The pronoun** 'them' **changes to** 'you'.**
 
• If the reporting verb is in the present tense or future tense, there will be no change in the tense/time/place of the reported speech.
 
• **'Am' **is used with first person singular pronoun. It is used with the pronoun, **'I'**.
 
• In the given sentence, the reporting verb is in the present tense so, there will be no change in its reported speech.
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 2.

 

**Correct sentence**__**:** *The secretary says to the audience, “I am going to help you.”*

questions.question:
**Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

My cafe has been revisited by many tourists.

options.text: Many tourists did revisited my cafe.
Many tourists have revisited my cafe.
Many tourists has revisited my cafe.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Many tourists have revisited my cafe."**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the present perfect tense.
 
• Passive Voice sentences of Present Perfect Tense use “has/have” along with “been” as a helping verb with respective number nouns and pronouns.
 
• Sentence structure:
 
 
• Passive: Object + has/have + been + V3 + by + subject.
 
• Active: Subject + has/have + V3 + object.
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• Passive: Food has been cooked by Reema. 
 
• Active: Reema has cooked food.
 
 
 
• The places of object and subject will be interchanged.
 
• **'has been revisited'** will be changed into '**have visited**'. 'have' will be used as '**tourists**' is plural.
 
• Thus, the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice is option 3. 

 

**Correct sentence:**__ *Many tourists have revisited my cafe.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

She said to me, “You will speak at the conference tomorrow.”

options.text: She told me that I would speak at the conference that day.
She told me that I might speak at the conference the next day.
She told me that I will speak at the conference the today.
She told me that I would speak at the conference the next day.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"She told me that I would speak at the conference the next day."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate correct indirect form of the sentence is** 'She told me that I would speak at the conference the next day.'**
 
• The given sentence is in the **future tense. **
 
• When the given sentence is in **future tense** in direct speech, it changes into **present conditional** in indirect speech.
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• **Direct:** She said, “I will be in Scotland tomorrow.”
 
• **Indirect:** She said that she would be in Scotland the next day.
 
 
 
• **'said to' **changes into** 'told' **as the reported verb has an object.
 
• The pronoun **'you' **changes to** 'I'.**
 
• **'will' **changes into **'would'.**
 
• **'tomorrow' **changes into** 'the next day'.**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4.**

**Correct Sentence:__ ***She told me that I would speak at the conference the next day.*

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__**

 
• The ‘future tense’ form of any verb refers to the conjugation of the verb to represent an action that will happen in the future or will continue in the future.
 
• The structure of the future tense is 
 
 
• *Subject + Will + Base form of the verb*
 
• Example: *Sindhu will walk to school tomorrow.*

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. It not only distances the addict from his/her social circles but also impacts their productivity badly.

B. People begin drinking just for the sake of it and gradually make it a habit.

C. Addiction of any kind, including alcoholic addiction impacts all aspects of an individual’s life.

D. Once it becomes a habit, it does not require much to change into an addiction.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"BDCA"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to order a meaningful and coherent paragraph is **'BDCA.'**
 
• Sentence **B** should come first as it is the introduction of the paragraph.
 
• Sentence **D** should come second as it explains what happens once drinking becomes a habit.
 
• Sentence **C** should come third as it tells about addiction in general and that it impacts all aspects of an individual’s life.
 
• Sentence **A** should come last as it explains the impacts of addiction.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3.**

 ​

**Correct Sequence:**__ *People begin drinking just for the sake of it and gradually make it a habit. Once it becomes a habit, it does not require much to change into an addiction. Addiction of any kind, including alcoholic addiction impacts all aspects of an individual’s life. It not only distances the addict from his / her social circles but also impacts their productivity badly.*

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'wealthy'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wealthy** means** someone has a great deal of money or is rich**.

 
 
• *Example - The society seems to favor only the **wealthy **and powerful. *
 
 
 
• Since the king needed finances, it makes sense that he sold the titles to wealthy candidates to gain wealth.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

Correct Passage:__ *The British king, Charles I, had (1) __inherited__ a very difficult financial situation from his father. His period saw a very high rate of inflation. He wanted to (2) __raise__ money. Therefore, he (3) __started__ creating the title of Baronet and selling it to **(4) __wealthy__** candidates. However, his decision was (5) ______ by the British parliament.*

• **Wealthy **stresses the possession of property and intrinsically valuable things.
 
• **Opulent **suggests lavish expenditure and display of great wealth, **more often applying to things than people.**
 
• The given sentence means that Charles I started creating the title of Baronet and selling it to people who possessed property and intrinsically valuable things.
 
• **Wealthy **is the most appropriate answer.
